d: A reproducible evaluation framework that measures recall, QPS, and build time for ANN implementations across fixed datasets (deep-image-96, sift-128) under standardized query budgets.
Computing embedding for data point and measuring distance to cluster centroid; large distance flags anomalous behavior.
An ANN algorithm that trades exact recall for sub-linear query time by probabilistically organizing the embedding space into clusters or graphs.
A retrieval query that returns an approximate set of nearest neighbors rather than exact results, trading guaranteed recall for reduced query latency and lower computational cost.
A quantization scheme using both scale_factor and zero_point to map an arbitrary [min, max] float range to the integer domain, enabling better utilization of the quantization range.
The relationship where a scoped API key grants authenticated access to a specific Pinecone project and its resources.
The process of periodically snapshotting a vector database's index files and payload state to durable object storage for restoration in the event of data loss or corruption.
The process of running multiple inputs through an embedding model simultaneously in a single forward pass to maximize GPU throughput and reduce per-item latency.
The containment relationship indicating a record resides within a specific Pinecone index for storage and retrieval.
The tenancy relationship indicating a record is scoped to a particular namespace within a Pinecone index.
An embedding model that independently encodes a query and a document into vectors, then computes similarity via a fast distance metric; enables pre-computed document vectors.
Okapi Best Matching 25: a probabilistic sparse retrieval model that scores documents by term frequency and inverse document frequency with length normalization.
Lexical baseline using term frequency and document length normalization; complements dense retrieval for exact-match queries.
The destructive overwriting of previously learned semantic relationships when an embedding model is fine-tuned on new data without regularization against the old embedding distribution.
An open-source embedded vector database written in Python; designed for developer simplicity with in-memory or persistence mode, commonly used in LLM and RAG applications.
The primary Python API client for Chroma; wraps HTTP or in-memory transport to a Chroma server or persistence layer.
A named namespace within Chroma that stores embeddings, associated documents, metadata, and IDs as an isolated group.
The similarity measure used for nearest-neighbor ranking; Chroma supports cosine, euclidean, and dot product distances.
The raw text or payload string that is embedded and stored alongside its vector representation in a collection.
A dense vector of floating-point numbers produced by an embedding function, representing the semantic position of a document in high-dimensional space.
A callable that converts raw input documents into embedding vectors; Chroma supports multiple backends (sentence-transformers, OpenAI, Cohere, etc.).
A unique identifier string assigned to each embedded document within a collection; used for targeted get/delete operations.
A metadata predicate applied at query time to restrict which entries are considered during approximate nearest-neighbor search.
An ephemeral Chroma instantiation where all data lives in process memory with optional snapshot-to-disk; no server required.
Structured key-value attributes attached to an embedding entry; enables filtering and payload queries at query time.
The mechanism for checkpointing collection state to disk; Chroma writes SQLite and binary files to a configurable root directory.
A search request containing a query vector (or text to embed) plus optional top-k and metadata filter parameters.
The ordered list of matches returned by a query, containing entry IDs, documents, metadata, and distance scores.
A long-running Chroma process that exposes a REST or gRPC API, managing one or more collections for remote clients.
The process of splitting a long document into smaller text segments (sentences, paragraphs, or fixed token windows) before embedding each chunk as a discrete vector.
A boundary value defining where outliers are clipped during quantization; values beyond the threshold are mapped to the quantization range extrema, introducing bounded error.
An unsupervised partitioning of the embedding space into k groups such that vectors within a cluster share geometric or semantic proximity.
An evaluation metric for embedding space organization measured by silhouette score, Davies-Bouldin index, or cluster purity against a labeled ground-truth partition of the data.
Model producing per-token vectors; retrieval uses MaxSim operator (max over token similarities) enabling fine-grained phrase matching.
A recommendation approach that learns joint user-item embedding vectors from interaction history, capturing latent taste factors without requiring explicit item content features.
A change in the statistical properties of the input data distribution that causes an embedding model trained on historical data to produce suboptimal representations for new inputs.
The configuration relationship where a distance metric parameterizes the similarity measure of a Pinecone index.
The concurrency and staleness guarantees provided by a distributed vector database: strong consistency requires all replicas to agree before returning, while eventual consistency allows stale reads.
The gating relationship where a filter expression restricts query results to records matching indexed scalar field conditions.
The composition relationship where a Pinecone record embeds dense vector values representing semantic embeddings for ANN search.
The organizational relationship where a Pinecone project holds one or more indexes as its primary data collections.
The composition relationship where a Pinecone record optionally embeds sparse vector dimensions for hybrid dense-sparse retrieval.
A recommendation approach that encodes item attributes into embedding vectors and retrieves items with embeddings similar to a user profile embedding.
A model adaptation paradigm that incrementally learns new concepts while preserving performance on previously learned ones, addressing the stability-plasticity dilemma in evolving embedding spaces.
A self-supervised training objective that pulls semantically similar pairs of embeddings together while pushing dissimilar pairs apart in the vector space.
A scalar similarity measure equal to the cosine of the angle between two vectors; range [-1, 1], with 1 indicating identical direction in the embedding space.
The provisioning relationship where an index creation operation establishes a new named vector collection with specified configuration.
A neural model that takes a query-document pair as a concatenated input and outputs a relevance score; more accurate than bi-encoder but too slow for first-stage retrieval.
The process of detecting and eliminating near-duplicate or exact-duplicate embedding vectors from a vector database to reduce storage waste and retrieval noise.
The removal of a specific vector and its associated metadata from a vector database, with behavior varying from immediate physical removal to soft-delete with periodic compaction.
Soft-delete approach: mark vector as inactive in metadata; physical removal deferred to periodic index compaction.
The use of dense bi-encoder embeddings to retrieve relevant text passages from a corpus, typically trained with contrastive loss on question-answer pairs.
A vector representation where most or all dimensions carry meaningful non-zero values, in contrast to sparse one-hot or bag-of-words encodings.
The reverse operation converting int8 back to float32 for computation; performed as (int8_value * scale_factor) + zero_point for asymmetric, or int8_value * scale_factor for symmetric.
Technique (PCA, UMAP, t-SNE) mapping high-dimensional embeddings to lower dimensions for visualization or efficiency.

A family of techniques (PCA, UMAP, autoencoders) that project high-dimensional embedding vectors into a lower-dimensional space while preserving pairwise distance structure for visualization or compression.
A sharded or replicated deployment of a vector database across multiple nodes to achieve horizontal scalability, with query routing and result merge across partition boundaries.
A single dense vector that summarizes the semantic content of an entire document, computed by pooling token-level embeddings or aggregating sentence-level vectors.
The process of adjusting a generic embedding model so that its learned representations better capture the semantic structure of a specific domain or vocabulary.
An inner-product similarity computed as the sum of element-wise products between two vectors; when vectors are L2-normalized it is equivalent to cosine similarity.
Raw inner product of unnormalized vectors; correlates with cosine similarity but is magnitude-sensitive.
A vector representation of a graph edge or relationship, often computed as a function (e.g., Hadamard product, concatenation) of the two endpoint node embeddings.
The dense vector field type and kNN search capability added to Elasticsearch 8.0+; supports cosine and dot-product similarity with approximate HNSW indexing.
A heuristic for selecting the optimal number of clusters in k-means by identifying the bend point in a plot of within-cluster sum of squares (WCSS) versus k.
A dense vector representation of data (text, image, audio) produced by a neural model that encodes semantic meaning into a numerical array.
A method for combining multiple embedding vectors (from document chunks, sentences, or modalities) into a single representative vector through averaging or weighted summation.
Microservice exposing trained embedding model via HTTP/gRPC; handles batching, caching, and model versioning independently of the DB.
A key-value store (Redis, memcached, disk) that persists computed embedding vectors to avoid redundant model inference for identical or duplicate inputs.
The length of the numerical vector produced by an embedding model; higher dimensions capture richer semantic nuance but increase storage, index size, and compute cost.

The gradual shift in embedding vector distributions over time as the underlying embedding model is retrained or the data semantics evolve, causing previously indexed vectors to become misaligned with fresh queries.
Adapting a pretrained embedding model to a specific domain or task via contrastive or triplet loss on labeled data.
A trained neural network that converts raw tokens or image patches into fixed-length dense vectors in the embedding space.
The process of choosing an optimal embedding model (BERT, OpenAI ada, SBERT, CLIP) based on dimension budget, latency constraints, retrieval quality benchmarks, and licensing constraints.
The process of scaling embedding vectors to unit Euclidean length; enables cosine similarity to be computed as a simple dot product between normalized vectors.
An end-to-end data processing workflow that ingests raw content, applies preprocessing, chunks text into segments, and produces embedding vectors for storage in the vector database.
An evaluation of how well an embedding space captures target semantic relationships, measured by downstream task accuracy, clustering quality metrics, or similarity probe benchmarks.
The infrastructure layer that exposes an embedding model as a low-latency HTTP or gRPC API, typically with batching, GPU inference, and horizontal scaling.
A dense vector representation of a real-world entity (person, place, organization) learned jointly with other entities in a knowledge graph or recommendation embedding table.
The L2 geometric distance between two embedding vectors computed as the square root of the sum of squared dimension differences; smaller values indicate greater similarity.
A brute-force scan of all vectors in a database to return provably correct nearest neighbors; prohibitively expensive at scale but used as the ground truth for evaluating ANN quality.
The inheritance relationship where pod-based and serverless deployment models specialize the base Pinecone index concept with distinct compute strategies.
Meta's open-source C++/Python library for dense vector similarity search; implements IVF, PQ, HNSW, ONNG, and GPU-accelerated kernels with optional 8-bit quantization.
The fraction of retrieved nearest neighbors that are not true nearest neighbors; a key metric for evaluating the quality of approximate nearest neighbor search results.
The continued training of a pre-trained embedding model on a domain-specific dataset to improve its ability to distinguish relevant semantic relationships in a targeted use case.
The 32-bit IEEE floating-point representation of a vector element prior to quantization; each value occupies 4 bytes and spans the full numerical range of float32.
A reduced-precision format that stores embedding dimensions as 16-bit IEEE half-precision floats, halving storage while maintaining near-fp32 retrieval quality for most embedding models.
A system property measuring how recently the vector database reflects the current state of the indexed corpus; affected by indexing latency, batch size, and incremental update frequency.
The use of graphics processing units to parallelize ANN computations (HNSW search, IVF scanning, PQ distance) achieving orders-of-magnitude throughput improvements over CPU-only implementations.
An index structure that models the embedding space as a navigable proximity graph where edges connect nearest neighbor vectors at each layer.
A neural architecture that operates on graph-structured data by propagating and transforming embedding vectors along edges and through node aggregation layers.
A negative training example that is semantically similar to the anchor (e.g., same topic or category) and thus creates stronger discrimination pressure during contrastive training.
The mathematical n-dimensional Euclidean (or inner-product) space in which embedding vectors reside; dimensionality typically ranges from 64 to 4096.
Hierarchical Navigable Small World: a graph-based ANN index that builds a multi-layer skip-list of proximity graphs, enabling logarithmic-time greedy search from an entry point.
Hierarchical Navigable Small World graph; layered skip-list + NN graph enabling logarithmic-layer traversal then constant-time local search.
The hosting relationship where a cloud provider infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure) runs a Pinecone serverless index deployment.
A retrieval strategy that combines dense vector similarity search with sparse keyword-based retrieval (BM25) to capture both semantic nuance and exact term matching.
Minimum acceptable accuracy or recall rate below which results are unacceptable for the application
Choice among ANN index types HNSW IVF ANNOY LSH determined by data scale query patterns and accuracy requirements
Maximum acceptable index construction time constraining algorithm complexity and sampling choices
FAISS API selecting index type and factory string for automatic parameter defaults and memory estimates
Use of GPU kernels for index construction or querying requiring specific index types and memory layout
Hyperparameters governing HNSW construction and search efConstruction m and ef controlling graph density and traversal depth
Strategy combining multiple index types such as HNSW over PQ or IVF with scalar quantization to balance speed accuracy and memory
Inverted file index hyperparameters nlist clusters and nprobe probe counts controlling partition granularity and search scope
Available RAM or VRAM for index and raw vectors constraining quantization choices and index density
Systematic exploration of parameter space to find optimal recall speed trade off for given constraints
Maximum acceptable query response time constraining algorithm selection and pruning aggressiveness
Desired fraction of true nearest neighbors returned governing aggressiveness of search pruning and parameter tuning
Target queries per second rate constraining parallelization and batch processing strategy
Analysis of query distribution vector density and access patterns informing algorithm and parameter selection
A dense vector extracted from an image by a vision transformer, CNN backbone, or CLIP vision encoder.
A database design choice where vectors are never updated in place; changes are appended as new versioned records, eliminating concurrent-read/write conflicts in distributed index shards.
The implementation relationship where a Pinecone index provides approximate nearest neighbor search over stored vector collections.
The ability to insert new vectors into an existing ANN index without rebuilding the entire structure from scratch; supported variably by different index types.
The wall-clock time required to construct a vector index from a corpus; varies from seconds (IVFFlat) to minutes (HNSW with high M/efConstruction) for billion-scale datasets.
The disk or memory footprint of a built ANN index, typically expressed in bytes per stored vector and overhead factors from the index structure.
Choice and configuration of ANN algorithm (HNSW, IVF, ANNOY, LSH) and its parameters (ef, nlist, nprobe) governing recall/speed trade-off.
The raw dot product between two unnormalized vectors; used as a similarity score for models that produce vectors in a non-normalized space.
Post-training quantization that converts 32-bit floating-point embedding dimensions to 8-bit signed or unsigned integers, reducing memory footprint and enabling faster integer arithmetic.
The 8-bit signed integer result of scalar quantization, mapping the original float32 range onto [-128, 127] or the unsigned variant [0, 255]; occupies 1 byte per element.
The integration relationship where a vector database connects to embedding models to ingest, store, and search generated vector representations.
The inspection relationship where an operation retrieves index metadata including dimension, namespace record counts, and storage fullness metrics.
An index that partitions the vector space into Voronoi cells (clusters) and maintains an inverted list of vectors per cell centroid, enabling scope-limited search.
The partitive relationship where a dense or sparse vector constitutes one of the mandatory or optional fields of a Pinecone record.
Inverted File Index; clusters vectors into Voronoi cells via k-means; search prunes to nearest centroids then scans partitions.
A centroid-based clustering algorithm that iteratively assigns vectors to nearest centroids and updates centroids as the cluster mean; used to build IVF and PQ codebooks.
A set of learned dense vectors representing entities and relation types in a knowledge graph, enabling link prediction and reasoning via vector arithmetic.
A hashing scheme that maps similar vectors to the same hash bucket with high probability; variants include signed random projection (SRP) for cosine similarity and Hamming LSH for binary vectors.
The management relationship where a service (such as Pinecone) orchestrates vector storage, indexing, and querying infrastructure.
The L1 distance between two vectors computed as the sum of absolute dimension differences; useful for high-dimensional sparse embedding spaces.
Diversification technique penalizing results too similar to already-selected items; balances relevance against coverage in top-k lists.
RAM or VRAM required to hold index and vectors; quantization (PQ, int8) is the primary compression lever.
An I/O strategy where the vector index files are mapped into the process address space, allowing the operating system's virtual memory manager to handle paging of large indexes from disk.
The factor by which memory_footprint is reduced, expressed as original_bytes / quantized_bytes; scalar quantization achieves approximately 4x savings (32-bit to 8-bit).
Pre-filtering step applying structured attribute conditions (date, category) before or after vector similarity search.
An open-source cloud-native vector database developed by Zilliz; supports multiple ANN indexes (HNSW, IVF, DiskANN), GPU acceleration, and distributed shard/replica deployments.
The reconfiguration relationship where an operation adjusts index properties such as replica count, pod type, or serverless settings.
Embedding model trained on cross-lingual data enabling semantic similarity across languages in a shared vector space.
A shared embedding space where text and images (or other modalities) are projected into the same vector space enabling cross-modal retrieval.
Query operation returning the k closest vectors by a distance or similarity metric in embedding space.

A training strategy in contrastive embedding models that randomly selects unrelated examples as negatives; hard negatives are semi-hard examples within a proximity margin that provide stronger gradient signal.
The output tensor produced by the final hidden layer of a neural embedding model; the vector stored and indexed in the vector database.
A dense vector representation of a graph node learned by graph embedding methods such as DeepWalk, Node2Vec, or GraphSAGE for downstream node classification or link prediction.
A training strategy that continuously updates embedding model weights from incoming queries and feedback in real time without full retraining from the complete historical corpus.
A chunking configuration that preserves a configurable number of tokens from the end of one chunk at the start of the next chunk to reduce information loss at segment boundaries.
The isolation relationship where a namespace divides a shared index into tenant-scoped record collections without separate infrastructure.
Principal Component Analysis: a linear dimensionality reduction method that projects vectors onto the top k orthogonal axes of maximum variance in the embedding space.
A granularity variant where each channel (dimension) has its own scale_factor, reducing precision loss for tensors with heterogeneous value distributions across dimensions.
A granularity variant where a single scale_factor and optionally zero_point applies to all elements in an entire tensor or vector.
A PostgreSQL extension that adds vector data type, L2/inner-product/cosine distance operators, and IVFFlat/HNSW index support within the Postgres query planner.
A managed cloud vector database service that provides serverless ANN indexing, real-time upserts, filtering, and multi-tenancy with SLA-backed availability.
A scoped credential for authenticating REST or gRPC calls to a Pinecone project.
The infrastructure provider hosting a Pinecone serverless index: aws, gcp, or azure.
A read-only snapshot of a Pinecone index stored as a named artifact, used for backup or index cloning.
An index reconfiguration operation in Pinecone that adjusts replicas, pod type, or serverless settings.
An index provisioning operation in Pinecone that specifies name, dimension, metric, and pod or serverless configuration.
A write operation that removes records from a Pinecone index by id, filter, or namespace.
A Pinecone record component representing dense embedding values for ANN search.
An introspection operation that returns index metadata including dimension, count per namespace, and index fullness.
The fixed vector dimensionality of a Pinecone index, set at creation and immutable thereafter.
A configurable similarity measure in Pinecone: cosine, euclidean, or dotproduct.
A read operation that retrieves records by explicit id list from a Pinecone index.
A metadata filtering construct in Pinecone query that gates results via indexed scalar fields.
A Pinecone transport layer using gRPC for low-latency upsert and query operations.
A named searchable collection of vectors in Pinecone, configurable with dimension, metric, and pod/serverless settings.
A runtime state of a Pinecone index: Initializing, Ready, Initializing, Upgrading, Scaling, or Error.
A Pinecone isolation model using namespaces within a shared index to serve multiple tenants.
A tenant isolation boundary within a Pinecone index that partitions records without separate infrastructure.
A pod-based index deployment model in Pinecone using pre-allocated compute resources with configurable replicas.
The top-level organizational unit in Pinecone that scopes API keys, indexes, and billing.
An official Python SDK for Pinecone providing typed wrappers around REST and gRPC APIs.
A read operation that returns approximate nearest neighbors to a query vector with optional metadata filtering and namespace scoping.
The target vector submitted to Pinecone query for ANN retrieval.
A query variant in Pinecone returning all vectors within a given radius of a query vector.
A data unit in Pinecone containing id, dense vector values, optional sparse values, and key-value metadata.
The geographic availability zone for a Pinecone index or project.
A serverless index deployment model in Pinecone that auto-scales compute and storage without pod management.
The numeric proximity value returned with each Pinecone query result, interpreting the configured distance metric.
A service-level guarantee attached to a Pinecone project specifying availability and support terms.
A Pinecone record component representing sparse dimensions (token id + values) for hybrid retrieval.
The count of nearest neighbors returned per Pinecone query request.
A write operation that inserts or updates records in a Pinecone index by unique id.
The fraction of returned results that are genuine nearest neighbors; precision at k measures how clean the top-k list is in an ANN retrieval.
The fraction of the top-k retrieved results that are true nearest neighbors; a standard retrieval quality metric reported at k values like 1, 10, or 100.
The accuracy degradation resulting from mapping continuous float32 values to a discrete int8 representation; measured as mean squared error, cosine similarity drop, or recall degradation.
A vector quantization technique that splits a high-dimensional vector into subvectors, independently quantizes each subvector, and concatenates codes to form a compact representation.
An open-source vector similarity search engine with a Rust core; provides HNSW and SCAN indexing, payload filtering, quantization, and a gRPC-first API.
The difference between the original float32 value and the reconstructed value after dequantization; the primary source of precision_loss in scalar_quantization.
The end-to-end time to submit a query vector and receive an ordered list of nearest neighbor IDs from a vector database.
The full software pipeline that connects a vector database, an embedding model, a retrieval step, and a language model into an end-to-end RAG system with query parsing and response formatting.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation pattern: vector search fetches relevant context chunks, injected into LLM prompt to ground generation.
The data access relationship where fetch or query operations retrieve stored records from a Pinecone index by id or vector similarity.
The fraction of true nearest neighbors that appear within the result set returned by an approximate nearest neighbor search; a primary quality metric for ANN indexes.
The fraction of all true nearest neighbors that appear within the top-k results returned by an approximate search; k must be larger than the number of true neighbors to approach 100%.
The input relationship where a query operation accepts an embedding vector as the basis for nearest-neighbor similarity search.

A system that suggests relevant items to users based on learned embeddings of users and items, using vector similarity search to retrieve candidate items from a collaborative or content-based embedding space.
The duplication of vector index shards across multiple nodes to improve read throughput, fault tolerance, and geographic query latency without changing the logical data set.
A two-stage retrieval process where an initial ANN search produces a candidate set that is then re-scored by a more expensive but accurate cross-encoder model.
A generation architecture that retrieves relevant context vectors from a vector database at inference time and prepends the decoded context to the language model prompt to reduce hallucination.
The output relationship where a query operation yields relevance scores indicating how closely each result matches the query vector.
Floating-point values mapped to low-precision (e.g. int8); reduces memory 4x with modest accuracy loss.
The multiplicative factor used to convert float32 values to int8 and back; computed as (value_range_max - value_range_min) / (quantization_range_max - quantization_range_min).
The authorization relationship where a Pinecone project defines the boundary of access granted by an associated API key.
A caching strategy that stores query vectors alongside their results and answers new queries by finding the nearest cached vector rather than recomputing the full retrieval pipeline.
Splitting documents into segments sized for embedding (typically 256–1024 tokens) to maximize topical coherence per chunk.
An information retrieval paradigm that finds results based on semantic meaning rather than exact keyword overlap, enabled by embedding-based similarity in a vector database.
A dense vector that represents the semantic content of an individual sentence, produced by a sentence-transformer model and stored as a single record in the vector database.
Distributing vector collection across multiple nodes; strategies include semantic clustering (by embedding region) or random partitioning.
The horizontal partitioning of a vector collection across multiple database nodes based on a partitioning scheme (range, hash, or vector-space Voronoi cells) to distribute query load.
The operation of finding vectors in a database that are most semantically or geometrically similar to a given query vector.
Minimum score below which results are discarded; tuned per use case to balance recall against noise.
A text segmentation strategy that moves a fixed-length token window over a document with a configurable step size to produce overlapping chunks for embedding.
The preservation relationship where a collection captures a point-in-time read-only copy of an index for backup or cloning purposes.
A deletion strategy that marks a vector as inactive in the payload without immediately removing it from the ANN index; physical removal occurs during periodic garbage collection.
A vector representation with mostly zero values, typical of BM25-weighted or TF-IDF bag-of-words encodings; often used alongside dense vectors in hybrid search.
Process of determining optimal scale and offset values from a data distribution (often percentile-based).
Representative sample of vectors used to determine scale_factor and zero_point; must cover the distribution to minimize quantization_error.
Inverse transformation that reconstructs float approximations from quantized integers using scale and offset.
Target integer type for quantized values (e.g. int8, uint8); defines bit-width of stored representation.
Bit-packing scheme for storing quantized values contiguously; enables dense memory layout.
Quantization error (e.g. MSE) introduced by value rounding; trade-off against compression ratio.
Zero-point value added during quantization (often for signed int8 centering around 0); subtracted at decode.
Strategy for values exceeding the calibrated value_range; options include clipping, separate outlier scale, or exclusion from quantization.
Scalar quantization variant where scale_factor is computed per column/feature dimension; reduces quantization_error at cost of storing multiple scales.
Scalar quantization variant where one scale_factor applies to the entire tensor; simpler but less accurate for heterogeneous distributions.
Target bit-width for quantized representation (e.g., int8, int16, float16); determines memory_footprint reduction ratio.
Difference between original floating-point values and reconstructed values after dequantization; primary quality metric for scalar_quantization.
Behavior when an input value exceeds the representable range; values are clipped to min/max of target dtype.
Floating-point multiplier that maps original values to the quantized integer range; inverse applied at decode time.
Multiplier applied during dequantization; computed from calibration_data to map quantized integer back to floating-point.
Per-tensor vs per-dimension quantization scope; global uses one scale/offset for entire tensor.
Ratio of signal power to quantization_error power; used to assess quality loss from scalar_quantization relative to full-precision.
Observed min-max bounds of floating-point values across the tensor being quantized; determines scale_factor magnitude.
Integer offset used in asymmetric quantization; enables efficient storage of value ranges not centered at zero.
The online computation of embedding vectors from a continuous data stream as new items arrive, without requiring reprocessing of the entire existing corpus.
A quantization scheme where the float range is centered at zero and only a scale factor is used; the zero point is implicitly zero; maps [-max_abs, max_abs] to [-127, 127].
A dense vector generated from a textual input (word, phrase, sentence, document) by a transformer or sentence-transformer model.
The practice of initializing an embedding model from weights pre-trained on a large corpus and then adapting those weights to a target downstream task.
The transport relationship where the gRPC API layer carries query requests and responses between client and Pinecone index service.
The transport relationship where the gRPC API layer carries upsert requests and acknowledgments between client and Pinecone index service.
A training loss that penalizes embeddings where the distance between an anchor and a negative example is not sufficiently larger than the distance between the anchor and a positive example.

t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding: a non-linear dimensionality reduction method that emphasizes preservation of local neighborhood structure for visualization of high-dimensional embedding spaces.
Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection: a non-linear dimensionality reduction technique that preserves both local and some global topological structure and is faster than t-SNE at scale.
The replacement of an existing vector's embedding values or payload metadata, requiring the database to update the relevant index structures without full index reconstruction.
The algorithm relationship where a Pinecone query executes ANN search to efficiently return near neighbors rather than exact matches.
The tenancy relationship where a multi-tenant configuration employs namespaces to isolate tenant data within a shared index.
The process of determining the min and max values (or percentile-based thresholds) across a representative dataset to compute optimal scale_factor and zero_point.
A specialized database system optimized for storing, indexing, and searching high-dimensional vector embeddings by similarity.
Dense numerical representation of discrete data (text, image, audio) as a point in high-dimensional continuous space where geometric proximity encodes semantic similarity.
A data structure inside a vector database that enables fast approximate nearest neighbor retrieval over collections of embedding vectors.
Scaling embedding to unit L2 norm; makes cosine similarity equivalent to dot product and prevents magnitude from distorting similarity.
The process of mapping a high-precision embedding vector to a lower-precision representative codeword to reduce storage size and speed up distance computations.
The infrastructure layer that exposes a vector database as a query API, handling index routing, sharding, replication, and result aggregation across nodes.
The tracking of multiple embedding versions for the same logical record, enabling time-travel queries, rollback of noisy embeddings, and lineage tracking for debugging.
The projection of embedding vectors into 2D or 3D space for human inspection of clustering, separation, and outlier structure in the learned semantic space.
An open-source vector database with built-in module support for embedding models (transformers, CLIP), hybrid BM25-plus-vector search, and GraphQL API.
A simple embedding aggregation method that computes a convex combination of multiple vectors, optionally weighting chunks by their relevance score or local importance.
Vector representation of individual words; methods include word2vec (Skip-gram, CBOW) and GloVe; captures word co-occurrence statistics.
The abstraction relationship where the official Python client provides typed gRPC method wrappers for low-latency vector operations.
The abstraction relationship where the official Python client provides typed REST method wrappers for HTTP-based vector operations.
The data mutation relationship where upsert or delete operations modify the record set stored within a Pinecone index.
An additive offset applied in asymmetric quantization to shift the zero point of the float range onto an integer value, enabling exact representation of true zero.
